questions.stem: A 3-year-old with progressive pancytopenia shows the skin pigmentation change (left) and the bilateral thumb abnormality (right) pictured. These combined findings are most characteristic of which inherited bone marrow failure syndrome?

explanation.summary: Cafe-au-lait spots with focal hypopigmentation plus radial/thumb anomalies in a child with pancytopenia point to Fanconi anemia, an autosomal recessive DNA-repair defect. Diagnosis is confirmed by increased chromosomal breakage with cross-linking agents.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cafe-au-lait spots with focal hypopigmentation plus radial/thumb anomalies in a child with pancytopenia point to Fanconi anemia, an autosomal recessive DNA-repair defect. Diagnosis is confirmed by increased chromosomal breakage with cross-linking agents.

questions.stem: These clinical photographs show a devastating adverse effect that appears shortly after starting an anticoagulant, caused by thrombosis of small dermal vessels. What underlying mechanism explains this early complication?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Transient hypercoagulability from rapid depletion of proteins C and S before the procoagulant factors fall

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vitamin K deficiency causing capillary fragility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Direct cytotoxic drug effect on keratinocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Immune complex deposition within dermal vessels

explanation.summary: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis occurs because the short-half-life anticoagulant proteins C and S are depleted first, producing a transient hypercoagulable state that thromboses small vessels and infarcts the skin; patients with protein C or S deficiency are especially susceptible.
explanation.whyCorrect: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis occurs because the short-half-life anticoagulant proteins C and S are depleted first, producing a transient hypercoagulable state that thromboses small vessels and infarcts the skin; patients with protein C or S deficiency are especially susceptible.

questions.stem: These skin findings in a patient with a thrombotic microangiopathy result most directly from which underlying abnormality?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Bacterial septic embolization to the skin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased vascular permeability from histamine release

explanation.summary: The pinpoint petechiae and larger purpura seen here occur because consumption of platelets in microthrombi leaves too few platelets to seal small vessels, allowing bleeding into the skin.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pinpoint petechiae and larger purpura seen here occur because consumption of platelets in microthrombi leaves too few platelets to seal small vessels, allowing bleeding into the skin.

questions.stem: In this illustration of ADAMTS13 deficiency, why do platelets adhere and form thrombi within the small vessels?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excess fibrin mesh physically traps the platelets

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bacterial toxin activates the platelets

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complement deposition on endothelium triggers aggregation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uncleaved ultra-large vWF multimers persist and readily bind platelets

explanation.summary: Without ADAMTS13 activity the ultra-large vWF multimers are not broken down; they remain anchored to endothelium and capture circulating platelets, forming the vWF-platelet microthrombi of TTP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Without ADAMTS13 activity the ultra-large vWF multimers are not broken down; they remain anchored to endothelium and capture circulating platelets, forming the vWF-platelet microthrombi of TTP.

questions.stem: The arrowed cells on this blood smear are increased in number and each shows a normally segmented, multilobed (2-5 lobe) purple nucleus. An elevation of these cells that is not caused by a neoplasm most commonly reflects what?

explanation.summary: The arrowed cells are mature segmented neutrophils. Benign mature neutrophilia most often occurs in response to bacterial infection or inflammation; other triggers include stress, smoking, and corticosteroids. Allergic/parasitic causes drive eosinophilia and viral infections drive lymphocytosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: The arrowed cells are mature segmented neutrophils. Benign mature neutrophilia most often occurs in response to bacterial infection or inflammation; other triggers include stress, smoking, and corticosteroids. Allergic/parasitic causes drive eosinophilia and viral infections drive lymphocytosis.

questions.stem: This neutrophil shows abnormally increased numbers of dark-staining cytoplasmic granules, giving them roughly the same color as the nucleus. These abnormal granules represent increased numbers of what?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Primary (azurophilic) granules containing peroxidases and hydrolases

explanation.summary: This is toxic granulation, a toxic change in which primary granules laden with peroxidases and hydrolases increase and stain darkly. It typically signals bacterial infection. Rough-ER remnants would be Dohle bodies and clear spaces would be vacuolization.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is toxic granulation, a toxic change in which primary granules laden with peroxidases and hydrolases increase and stain darkly. It typically signals bacterial infection. Rough-ER remnants would be Dohle bodies and clear spaces would be vacuolization.

questions.stem: In addition to dark toxic granules, this neutrophil contains small clear spaces within its cytoplasm. These clear spaces arise from which process, and are most classically seen in which clinical setting?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fat accumulation from a metabolic disorder

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rough ER remnants left after protein synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Degranulation of lysosomes, seen in sepsis

explanation.summary: Cytoplasmic vacuolization results from degranulation of lysosomes as neutrophils destroy pathogens, and is most typical of sepsis with widespread intracellular pathogen destruction. It commonly accompanies toxic granulation as another toxic change.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytoplasmic vacuolization results from degranulation of lysosomes as neutrophils destroy pathogens, and is most typical of sepsis with widespread intracellular pathogen destruction. It commonly accompanies toxic granulation as another toxic change.

questions.stem: This smear shows enlarged, irregularly shaped lymphocytes with voluminous, deeply basophilic cytoplasm. Such reactive lymphocyte changes are most classically associated with which of the following?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Viral infection such as infectious mononucleosis (EBV)

explanation.summary: Reactive lymphocytes are larger than normal with abundant, sometimes dark blue cytoplasm and can be bilobed. They are seen primarily in viral infections such as EBV (infectious mononucleosis), CMV, and viral hepatitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reactive lymphocytes are larger than normal with abundant, sometimes dark blue cytoplasm and can be bilobed. They are seen primarily in viral infections such as EBV (infectious mononucleosis), CMV, and viral hepatitis.

questions.stem: This large lymphocyte has abundant agranular cytoplasm that abuts and molds around the adjacent red cells, giving a 'fried egg' appearance. This cell type is most strongly associated with which virus?

explanation.summary: This is a Downey type II cell, the most common form of reactive lymphocyte, characteristically linked to Epstein-Barr virus infection (infectious mononucleosis). Its abundant cytoplasm molds around neighboring erythrocytes, producing the fried-egg look.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is a Downey type II cell, the most common form of reactive lymphocyte, characteristically linked to Epstein-Barr virus infection (infectious mononucleosis). Its abundant cytoplasm molds around neighboring erythrocytes, producing the fried-egg look.

questions.stem: This patchy, scaly, erythematous rash on sun-protected skin of the trunk is the earliest cutaneous manifestation of mycosis fungoides. This lesion type represents which stage of the disease?

explanation.summary: Flat, scaly, erythematous macules/patches, often in a bathing-suit distribution, are the earliest (patch-stage) lesions of mycosis fungoides and are frequently misdiagnosed as eczema or psoriasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Flat, scaly, erythematous macules/patches, often in a bathing-suit distribution, are the earliest (patch-stage) lesions of mycosis fungoides and are frequently misdiagnosed as eczema or psoriasis.

questions.stem: This raised, thick, red cutaneous lesion is more advanced than a simple scaly patch of mycosis fungoides. Which stage of the disease does it represent?

explanation.summary: As mycosis fungoides progresses, flat patches thicken into raised, indurated, red plaques (plaque stage) before evolving into frank nodular tumors.
explanation.whyCorrect: As mycosis fungoides progresses, flat patches thicken into raised, indurated, red plaques (plaque stage) before evolving into frank nodular tumors.

questions.stem: These large, nodular, mushroom-like growths on the skin are the feature that gave this lymphoma its name. Which stage of mycosis fungoides is shown?

explanation.summary: Nodular, exophytic 'fungating' tumors define the advanced tumor stage of mycosis fungoides and are the origin of the name (fungus-like).
explanation.whyCorrect: Nodular, exophytic 'fungating' tumors define the advanced tumor stage of mycosis fungoides and are the origin of the name (fungus-like).

questions.stem: This diffuse, red, scaling, peeling eruption involving more than 80% of the body surface, occurring in the leukemic phase of a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, is a defining feature of which condition?

explanation.summary: Sezary syndrome is the leukemic/erythrodermic variant of mycosis fungoides, defined by the triad of diffuse erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy, and clonal cerebriform (Sezary) cells in skin, nodes, and blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sezary syndrome is the leukemic/erythrodermic variant of mycosis fungoides, defined by the triad of diffuse erythroderma, generalized lymphadenopathy, and clonal cerebriform (Sezary) cells in skin, nodes, and blood.

questions.stem: In this skin biopsy, the circled intraepidermal cluster of atypical lymphocytes is a hallmark histologic finding of mycosis fungoides. What is this feature called?

explanation.summary: Intraepidermal collections of neoplastic T lymphocytes are called Pautrier microabscesses; despite the name they contain lymphoma cells, not neutrophils, and are characteristic of mycosis fungoides.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intraepidermal collections of neoplastic T lymphocytes are called Pautrier microabscesses; despite the name they contain lymphoma cells, not neutrophils, and are characteristic of mycosis fungoides.
